title: Jal Jeevan Mission
subtitle: Enabling India's Rural Water Infrastructure with Real-Time Monitoring
hero_summary: Rugged industrial M2M gateways enabled real-time monitoring and remote automation of geographically distributed rural water infrastructure under India's Jal Jeevan Mission — bridging legacy Modbus field devices with cloud-based telemetry platforms over secure 4G/LTE networks. Extended to irrigation infrastructure with solar-powered deployments supporting remote pumping stations and canal automation.
challenge:
Water supply departments required reliable telemetry across thousands of rural pumping stations and irrigation sites under extreme constraints:


• Intermittent grid power with frequent outages and severe voltage fluctuations

• No fiber connectivity — nearest ISP termination many kilometers away

• Large-scale deployment across thousands of remote sites needing uniform configuration

• Difficult terrain access and high site visit costs (hours of travel)

• Solar-powered remote sites requiring battery autonomy and low-power operation

• Unmanned operation with regional-language operators and minimal technical training
solution: Tenet's rugged industrial M2M Cellular Gateway deployed with integrated protocol conversion engine capable of translating Modbus RTU/TCP data into MQTT streams over secure 4G/LTE connectivity. Local data buffering ensured continuity during intermittent connectivity conditions. Solar-powered deployment compatibility enabled remote irrigation infrastructure connectivity without grid power dependency.
impact: Two-way secure communication enabled remote pump control and automation
Existing PLCs and field sensors remained operational without hardware replacement
Reduced deployment complexity and rollout costs significantly
Improved visibility into distributed rural water and irrigation infrastructure
Enhanced operational continuity during network instability
Successfully deployed across Rajasthan, Maharashtra, and Uttarakhand
Supported irrigation automation in rural and semi-urban agricultural regions

title: Smart Cities
subtitle: Powering Urban Safety and Intelligence for Smart City Infrastructure
hero_summary: Outdoor industrial M2M gateways enabled secure connectivity between traffic systems, ANPR enforcement, surveillance infrastructure, and Integrated Command & Control Centers (ICCCs) across urban and peri-urban smart city deployments.
challenge:
Smart city operators needed a resilient backbone for traffic, ANPR, surveillance, and ICCC systems under real-world urban constraints:


• Roadside cabinet installations with extreme heat, vibration, and dust

• Frequent fiber cuts during monsoons and construction

• Outer city/highway corridors with no wired backhaul available

• 24/7 zero-downtime expectations across hundreds of locations

• Distributed deployment requiring centralized remote management

• ISP outages lasting hours to days during severe weather
solution: Tenet deployed rugged outdoor M2M gateways with secure 4G/5G connectivity, multi-WAN failover, and centralized remote management connecting traffic signals, surveillance cameras, ANPR systems, public alert systems, environmental monitoring equipment, and edge processing units to centralized ICCC infrastructure.
impact: Enabled automated traffic enforcement and live surveillance at hundreds of locations
Extended connectivity into outer city limits and highway corridors without wired backhaul
Reduced field maintenance effort through centralized management
Enabled real-time diagnostics, monitoring, and OTA firmware upgrades
Improved operational visibility for smart city administrators
Continuous city-wide monitoring even during ISP outages

title: City Gas Distribution
subtitle: Empowering City Gas Networks with Secure, Always-On Connectivity
hero_summary: Industrial M2M gateways enabled secure telemetry and centralized monitoring across city gas distribution infrastructure — connecting gas flow meters, pressure sensors, and SCADA systems over resilient multi-operator cellular networks.
challenge:
City Gas Distribution operators required secure, highly reliable communication across hazardous and remote pipeline infrastructure:


• Unmanned remote stations with no local technical support

• 24/7 uptime requirements — zero tolerance for communication failures

• Legacy RS232/RS485 equipment needing protocol bridging

• Wide geographical distribution spanning hundreds of kilometers

Enabled real-time anomaly detection and pressure monitoring
Reduced manual maintenance and field configuration effort
Improved security through encrypted communications
Simplified large-scale operational management using centralized updates
